I'm **{{< var personal.name >}}**, a {{< var personal.role >}} in the {{< var personal.affiliation >}}.

My doctoral work asks how social contact, mobility and attitude data can be used
to understand and forecast the behavioural drivers of epidemic dynamics — the
messy, human half of why outbreaks unfold the way they do. It builds on a
background in mathematics and health data science, and on earlier work using
branching process models to estimate the probability that an introduction
becomes a major epidemic.

Alongside that I work in health economics, on cost-utility modelling and
economic evaluation of blood-borne virus screening interventions: coding
hepatitis B progression models, evaluating TB IGRA testing in high-risk groups,
and micro-costing digitally enhanced BBV testing.
